pageTitle: Soccer Tactics Simulator - Free Tactic Animation Web App | GetNiftyKit
metaDescription: A free web tool that turns your board into a moving tactic animation as you move players and the ball frame by frame. Curved runs, auto-save, .json and .mp4 export, no install, no sign-up.
softwareAppDescription: A free web tool for soccer coaches to record player and ball movement frame by frame on a timeline, build tactic animations, share .json files with the coaching staff, and export .mp4 video for parents and players.
fsHint: Press again or hit ESC to close the full window.
fsOpenAria: Open the simulator in a full window
subtitle: Record player and ball movement frame by frame to build a tactic animation
taglineExtra: You can operate the board right below, and every tactic auto-saves in your browser so it's still there next time you open it.
infoIntroP: Soccer Tactics Simulator lets you place your team, the opposing team, and the ball on a vertical pitch, then move them at each frame (moment) of the bottom timeline. The frames connect automatically into a moving tactic animation. You can rotate each player's facing direction, and drag the yellow dot on a movement path to switch from a straight run to a curved one. Every tactic auto-saves in your browser, can be exported as a .json file to share with or load from other coaches, and where supported can also be saved as .mp4 video. It's a free tool you open straight in the browser with no sign-up and no install.
infoHowtoP: First pick a frame (moment) with the ◀ ▶ buttons at the bottom right or the slider below. At that moment, drag players and the ball to where you want them; the frame auto-saves the instant you let go. Move to the next frame and shift positions again — repeat, and the two frames connect into an animation. Use the ▶ play button to review the movement, and change playback speed and looping in Settings. When you only want to record the current moment as a keyframe without moving anything, press the ➕ button.
infoUseCases: When you want to explain set pieces and build-up patterns as moving diagrams before a training session
When the coaching staff wants to pass tactic files (.json) around and discuss the same screen together
When you want to share tactical movement with parents and players as a short video (.mp4)
When you'd rather draw and save a tactics board straight in a tablet or PC browser instead of on a whiteboard

faq.q: Where are the tactics I make saved?
faq.a: As you edit, each tactic auto-saves to the local storage of the browser you're using. Open the same browser again and the last tactic you were viewing opens as-is; pick another tactic from the library and it saves to that one. It isn't shared with other devices or browsers, so to move a tactic, export it as a .json file.

faq.q: Can I make a player's run curved?
faq.a: Yes. When you move a player, the movement path shows as a dashed line, and dragging the yellow dot on that line makes the run curved. Double-click the yellow dot to go back to a straight line.

Video export isn't supported in the browser, so it doesn't appear in the menu. On the web only .json save/load and auto-save are supported. Video saving is available in the Android, iOS, and macOS apps.
This tool uses a vertical pitch, so the layout is tall. You can zoom and pan inside the frame with your fingers (or mouse wheel / pinch), and to use it larger, open the frame in a new tab.

faq.q: Do I need to sign up?
faq.a: No. You can use it straight in the browser with no sign-up or login, and the tactics you enter are not sent to any server.

privacyNote: This tool keeps tactic data only in your browser's local storage and does not send it to any server.
